title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 22
paragraphs: These were the ones who undertook the task and were posted at Erythrai in advance of the other Greeks present, having chosen to take the archers with them. For some time, then, they fought, and at last the fighting was ended in the following way. While the cavalry was attacking by squadrons, the horse of Masistios, going in advance of the rest, was struck in the side by an arrow; in pain it reared upright and threw Masistios off. When he had fallen, the Athenians at once pressed upon him; they took his horse, and killed him as he resisted — though at first they could not, for his armor was such: under a crimson tunic he wore a cuirass of golden scales. As they struck the cuirass they could do nothing, until someone, seeing the problem, thrust into his eye. Then at last he fell and died. By chance the rest of the cavalry did not see this happen — they neither saw him fall from his horse nor saw him being killed — and as the retreat and the wheeling about were taking place, they did not perceive what was happening. But when they halted their horses, they immediately missed him, since there was no one to command them; and once they grasped what had happened, they passed the word to one another and all rode back together, so that they might, if possible, recover the body.
